question: An infinitely long straight wire carries a current of I. At what distance r from the wire is the magnetic field 5 × 10⁻⁶ T if I = 15 A?
solution: The correct answer is __0.6 m**(Option 1)**.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • Magnetic field__ around a long straight wire carrying current is given by B = (μ₀ I) / (2πr). • Here, B = 5 × 10⁻⁶ T, I = 15 A, and μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A. • Rearranging the formula for r: r = (μ₀ I) / (2πB). • Substitute the values: r = [(4π × 10⁻⁷) × 15] / [2π × (5 × 10⁻⁶)]. • Simplify: r = (60π × 10⁻⁷) / (10π × 10⁻⁶) = 0.6 m. • Hence, the distance from the wire where the magnetic field is 5 × 10⁻⁶ T is 0.6 m. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** • **Magnetic Field Lines:** • Magnetic field lines around a straight current-carrying wire are concentric circles. • The direction of the field is given by the **right-hand thumb rule.** • **Right-Hand Thumb Rule:** • It states that if the thumb of the right hand points in the direction of the current, then the curled fingers show the direction of the magnetic field. • **Applications of Magnetic Field:** • Used in electromagnets, electric motors, and generators. • Helps in understanding electromagnetic wave propagation. 7e:Tbcc,
